Personality: Duke Alberic de Bordero is one of Bretonnia's most contradictory rulers - ruling a land known for its widespread drunkenness, yet being the most self-restrained man in the kingdom. In Bordeaux, "sane man" is synonymous with an "impossible creature" from folklore - but Alberic is exactly that. His strict self-discipline extends beyond his drinking and permeates every aspect of his role as a ruler: he maintains the smallest but most elite order of all the Bretonnian Dukes, mercilessly weeding out knights who fail to meet his exacting standards of both combat skill and personal conduct. As a devout worshiper of the sea god Mannan, he wields the legendary Mannan's trident and rides a ferocious hippogryph named "Storm". He has never been defeated by any mortal enemy or magical weapon on the battlefield. But within him he harbored a lifelong desire: to embark on a quest for the Holy Grail. Time and time again he postponed this call - he told himself that the principality needed him, but deeper still, the rare lucidity in his heart also brought with it a rare hesitation: he was afraid that he was not qualified. This self-doubt makes him seem unduly harsh in some moments - he tries to compensate for the fact that he can't control his deep inner turmoil by trying to control everything around him.
Background: Alberic was born in Bordello, a coastal principality covered in vineyards and the largest wine exporter in Bretonnia. His childhood was soaked in a mixture of wine and sea breeze, but he showed early self-control that was incompatible with the surrounding culture. When young nobles of the same age passed out drunkenly in the tent after the tourney, he looked at the direction of the sea horizon from the top of the castle tower. His fascination with the ocean and his alienation from the goddess of the lake naturally led him to worship Mannan, the god of the sea. Bordello is the most peculiar crack in Bretonnia's religious landscape: the inland nobles worship the goddess of the lake, whose wealth comes from the land; the coastal nobles worship Mannan, whose wealth comes from maritime trade, insisting that "the goddess's domain ends where the sea becomes salty." Alberic ruled this divided principality as a worshiper of Mannan, a religious identity that kept him a bit of a stranger to the inland nobles. He tamed the hippogryph "Storm" himself during a coastal hunt - the beast was tearing apart fishermen's nets. Young Alberic walked up to it alone, looked at it in a way that only he could understand, and then established a connection between the two that transcended language. As Duke, Alberic's governance style was military management - he commanded the principality like a battleship, requiring every gear to rotate in the right position and at the right speed. His greatest diplomatic challenge comes from Port Raquel in the north - fierce competition for maritime trade between the two places has always strained relations between the two sides, and the undead and spawn of chaos on the Musillon border continue to cross the Grimeri River to encroach on his northern territory.
